in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit in the UK.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm inquiring about one child. I have an 11-year-old named Alex that I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to determine eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This typically means either you live with Alex, or you're paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards their care (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me at the moment, but I do contribute towards their upkeep - I help with things like clothes, school expenses, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important point - when a child doesn't live with you, the amount and regularity of your contributions matters.

**Can you tell me approximately how much you contribute towards Alex's upkeep per week or per month? And has Alex been living away from you for more than 8 weeks?**

(For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, or £16.95 per week for additional children.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep. As for how long they've been living away from me - well, they haven't actually come to live with me yet. I'm in the process of adopting Alex, but they haven't moved in with me yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that - this is very helpful information! The adoption situation changes things.

**Has Alex come to live with you yet as part of the adoption process, even if the adoption isn't legally complete? Or are they still living elsewhere (for example, in foster care or with their birth family) while the adoption process is ongoing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't come to live with me yet. They're still living elsewhere while we're going through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I need to understand a bit more about Alex's current living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living? For example, are they in foster care with the local council involved, or are they living with relatives or their birth family?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They're living with their birth family at the moment while the adoption process goes through.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have one more important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? For example, is anyone in their birth family claiming it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while they're living with their birth family during the adoption process?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance.

## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While you are contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 for an only child), the specific rule for adoption states: **"You can claim Child Benefit as soon as any child you're adopting comes to live with you - you do not have to wait until the adoption process is complete."**

Since Alex has not yet come to live with you and is still living with their birth family during the adoption process, you cannot claim Child Benefit at this time.

**The good news:** Once Alex moves in with you as part of the adoption placement, you will be able to claim Child Benefit immediately - you won't need to wait for the adoption to be legally finalized. So as soon as Alex comes to live with you, you should make your claim.

I hope this helps clarify your situation, and I wish you all the best with your adoption of Alex!
